title: "Q2D cross-section extraction"
description: "Extract per-unit-length quantities from an explicitly defined uniform CPW section."
sidebar: simulation
---

## Purpose and selected cross-section

Calculate per-unit-length matrices for the finite-ground CPW cross-section.
The selected system consists of a Signal rectangle, two reference Ground
rectangles, a substrate and surrounding region, assumed uniform along the
line. Finite launchers, bends, resonator ends and three-dimensional contacts
are outside this model.

Use the section notebook's own geometry. Its dimensions are not automatically
the same as the finite 3D CPW coupon, so the two examples are not equivalent
merely because they share a family name.

## Geometry, reference and settings choices

State the section axes, rectangle extents, conductor thickness, material
records and substrate extent. Keep separated Ground rectangles assigned to
the intended reference group. Specify surrounding-region/exterior treatment,
requested matrix families and ordering.

This section is authored directly in two dimensions. It needs neither a
GDS import nor a three-dimensional port sheet or source/sink face assignment.
Extraction frequency and material treatment define the requested line
response; mesh and adaptive controls govern its numerical calculation.
Their exact values remain in the notebook.

::: {.callout-note}
Any impedance or propagation quantity must identify its source matrix,
per-length units and derivation convention. It is not a finite-device
transmission measurement.
:::

## Workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

A wave-port or mode calculation using Palace is a different formulation.
A comparison must explicitly match the section, material model and
per-length conventions rather than re-labeling mode output as Q2D extraction.

### AEDT

Use [Finite-ground CPW Q2D](../../notebooks/CrossSectionSimulation/CpwFiniteGround/aedt_q2d.ipynb).
Create the native section, inspect conductor/reference grouping and materials,
then extract the requested per-length matrices. Resolve the returned data
independently of the live section session.

:::

## Expected outputs

Retain native section dimensions, thicknesses, material assignments and
conductor grouping. Return frequency-labeled per-unit-length C/G and R/L
matrices with ordering, units and adaptive history. Include requested line
quantities with their explicit matrix reduction/derivation.

When comparing to a 3D model, identify the actual matched slice and the finite
effects intentionally excluded. This page creates no new section dimensions
or cross-model agreement threshold.
